objective: Replace the preservation runtime's synthetic signed JSON boundary with execution-derived receipts issued by a protected attestor, while keeping all external effects denied.
invariants: The attestor never signs caller-authored probe semantics; only a live runner result can be consumed.

Every receipt binds one pre-execution challenge, unit, contract, scope and binding epoch, work revision, lifecycle stage, repository subject, runner, adapter, executable argv, exit outcome, raw-output digests, allowlisted result IDs, expiry, and credential epoch.
Baseline execution uses a sealed immutable Git tree and completion execution uses a sealed current workspace snapshot with pre/post identity checks.
Planning evidence cannot satisfy completion, and every four-role stage requires two consecutive clean executions per role.

Execution is read-only and without network; filesystem writes are limited to attestor-owned scratch, and sockets, service-manager calls, messages, publication, and every other external effect remain denied rather than brokered by this change.

Linux uses a protected OS identity, immutable installed worker, service-owned key and store, and a pinned bubblewrap sandbox; an unsupported, unavailable, or unprovisioned platform remains REVIEW_ONLY.

Repository receipt JSONL remains audit-only; request-contract accepts only a short-lived evidence-set decision signed after the attestor verifies its protected SQLite ledger and a root-owned verifier manifest.

A dedicated preservation credential, key epoch, runner allowlist, adapter allowlist, installed execution core, and snapshot core are pinned in root-owned policy and never reused from the review runner.

The attestor API accepts identifiers only; it requires a root-policy preregistration instead of trusting first use, creates each challenge, executes actual product modules or CLI, persists terminal state, rematerializes the current subject at seal, and seals the complete baseline/current set itself.

modules.result: Sealed real-entry execution and signed receipt issuance under a dedicated OS identity, service-owned credential and store, and pinned build epoch
modules.verification: Positive Linux isolated-service run plus same-UID, forged, replayed, drifted, wrong-stage, wrong-command, timeout, signal, symlink, and result-substitution tests. Missing service isolation, key ownership, pinned worker, or sandbox fails closed.

modules.result: The exact ten Discord contract surfaces execute through baseline/current production modules or CLI with challenge-bound exact observations
modules.verification: Generic nonzero exits, guard errors, extra output, wrong challenge, unknown capability IDs, ambient config/DB use, no-op substitutions, and surface-set drift all fail.

modules.result: Request-contract reads one protected-key evidence-set decision for the active binding and keeps every external effect blocked.
modules.verification: Two complete four-role rounds are required in round-major order; intervening DIRTY reviews invalidate the seal; missing or stale attestor receipts keep delivery REVIEW_ONLY; shell, service, network, message and publication paths remain blocked.

modules.result: Provisioning and rollback are explicit operator steps; absence of the protected OS service is observable and never downgraded to a local signer.
modules.verification: A same-user key, caller-supplied public key, environment private key, repository-owned policy, unpinned installed worker/core, unsupported platform, or unavailable service deterministically returns REVIEW_ONLY.

nonGoals: Treat a schema-valid signature as proof of execution
Allow arbitrary shell commands through regex classification
Implement or authorize external effects; they remain blocked for this change
Enable request-contract enforcement before the protected service, keys, and allowlists are provisioned
Expose private model reasoning or Discord message content
failureScenarios: A writer invokes a blind signer over fabricated output; prevented because the protected attestor accepts identifiers only and performs execution itself.
The worktree or adapter changes after hashing; prevented by sealed snapshots, post-run digest checks, and protected rematerialization immediately before and after seal signing.

A planning receipt or prior revision is replayed at release; prevented by root-policy preregistration, planning/current revision separation, challenge terminal state, receipt expiry, and a short-lived signed evidence-set decision.

reviewProtocol.releaseDecision: Request-contract validates the protected attestor evidence-set decision against a fixed root-owned public key and verifier manifest, and preserves REVIEW_ONLY whenever any required receipt or control is absent. Publication and deployment remain blocked until a protected external-effect broker consumes the decision.
